reader.requirement: At --std 85 a CANCEL must name a program callable from the cancelling program under the X.1.3.8.1 scope conventions, so its program-name must resolve exactly as a CALL from that program would (directly contained program first, then a visible COMMON program, then a separately compiled one); a name the source cannot call is a non-conforming program, for which the text sets no result.

edition-consulted.switches: edition spelling of the literal name

reader.edition-search: ResolveVisible and ProgramNameScope consult no edition (grep of DialectLevel, Edition, Year in ProgramTable.cs found only the GR5 parameter); its RECURSIVE arm cannot arise at 85
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: CANCEL resolves through the one CALL scope resolver at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf32_04 covers a COMMON program cancelled by its container and by a sibling; not exercised there: two programs with one name (contained and separately compiled), a COMMON program shadowing a separately compiled one, a name not callable from the cancelling program

probes.printed: NESTED DUP 1 / NESTED DUP 2 / OUTER DUP 1 / --- MAIN CANCEL DUP / NESTED DUP 1 / OUTER DUP 2 / HID 1 / --- SIB CANCEL HID / HID 1
probes.expected: CANCEL DUP from P3MAIN reaches the directly contained DUP (X.1.3.8.1 SR1, X.5.2.4 GR4a), not the separately compiled DUP

probes.printed: NESTED CMN 1 / NESTED CMN 2 / OUTER CMN 1 / --- CA CANCEL CMN / NESTED CMN 1 / OUTER CMN 2
probes.expected: from CA the COMMON sibling CMN is the callable one (X.1.3.8.1 SR2, X.5.2.4 GR4b) and is the one cancelled

probes.printed: HID 1 / --- MAIN CANCEL HID / HID 2; then CANCEL of its own separately compiled container from P10IN: abnormal run-unit termination EC-PROGRAM-CANCEL-ACTIVE citing §1985:X.5.3.4 GR5
probes.expected: rule violated (name not callable): no result specified; a not-located name is GR8's no action, and the container case also breaks GR5

OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.1 SR1  (1.3.8.1 Conventions for Program-Names)  the text is in SR1
OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.1 SR2  (1.3.8.1 Conventions for Program-Names)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: GR3 constrains the source; the compiler meets it by resolving CANCEL through the same scope resolver as CALL, and probes show the right program of a duplicated name is cancelled. ResolveVisible's outermost arm does not apply X.1.3.8.1 rule 3's exception (a program cannot reference its own separately compiled container), but such a CANCEL also breaks GR5 and is refused at run time, so no conforming program is affected.

refuter.evidence: Aimed at the case the reader did not try: a non-COMMON sibling of the cancelling program with the same name as a separately compiled program, where X.5.2.4 GR4c sends CALL and CANCEL to the separately compiled program. r6c_cancelscope.cob at --std 85: MAIN reaches its directly contained B ('NESTED NONCOMMON B 1'), A in MAIN reaches the separately compiled B ('SEPARATE B 1 / SEPARATE B 2'), 'A CANCEL B' cancels the separately compiled B ('SEPARATE B 1' on the next call) and leaves the nested B's state ('NESTED NONCOMMON B 2'); K cancels the COMMON X ('COMMON X 1' after the CANCEL). r6_cancelscope.cob: a directly contained X and a COMMON X inside one outermost program is refused (COBOL2214), which the 1985 X.1.3.8.1 text requires ('when two programs in a run unit are identically named, at least one of those two programs must be directly or indirectly contained within another separately compiled program which does not contain the other'); r6b: a call from K to a non-COMMON sibling R6TAIL ends EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND (not callable, SR1). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.5.3.4 GR3 ... the text is in GR3'; 'OK  §1985:X.5.2.4 GR4 ... the text is in GR4'; 'OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.1 SR1 ... the text is in SR1'. Read ProgramTable.cs#Cancel and #ResolveVisible: CANCEL resolves through the CALL resolver with probe: false, so a never-loaded separately compiled program is GR8's no action.
